- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts often peak too early or too low relative to true price acceleration.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after sharp spikes, underestimating the persistence of upward trends.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days and overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” effect after sharp declines — often underestimates the magnitude of recovery.
- When true prices show a clear upward trend, model forecasts lag behind and underestimate the slope.
- Model overestimates volatility in the middle of the forecast window, leading to over-sharp peaks and troughs.
